evidence.note: Reviewed the two new test files against the implementation they claim to pin (internal/fsm/cli/escalation.go, internal/fsm/sandbox/sandbox.go, internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:182-188) and against the consumer that acts on the result (internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:569-604). Method was mutation: an isolated copy of the tree in a scratch directory, `go test -count=1 ./internal/fsm/...` per mutant.

Mutants KILLED (guards genuinely pinned): neutering the '..' prefix check while keeping the strings import; dropping filepath.IsAbs; 0o444 -> 0o644; dropping sort.Strings; dropping base/head from the tree-hash header; dropping referencedByFindings from escalationFor; dropping judge.WithCodexWorkDir; dropping `scenario != nil` from ctxDeps.escalation. Those eight lines are all held by a test that fails when they change.

Mutants SURVIVED the full ./internal/fsm/... suite: deleting `|| code != 0` from changedPaths; deleting strings.ToLower from the codex prefix test; renaming the p.bools key in run.go:49; deleting the --no-escalate entry from boolFlags in run.go:88. Each survivor is reported as a finding below.

Independent probe tests (written in the scratch copy only, never in the repo) drove escalationFor with the exact tuple gate.RealExec returns for a git failure -- (out, stderr, nonzero, nil error) -- and compared the materialized bytes to the file on disk. Both probes failed, confirming findings 1-3 empirically rather than by reading.

The three lowered floors were checked arithmetically against measured statement counts at base (334e752, via git archive into scratch) and at head: internal/state 58 -> 53 statements, internal/runchain 107 -> 102, internal/findings 293 -> 288, with 50/58=86.2 -> 45/53=84.9, 99/107=92.5 -> 94/102=92.2 and 272/293=92.8 -> 267/288=92.7 all exact.

Prompt claims verified against code: testdata/fsm/agent-prompt.golden:36,44 carries the new text so the pinned golden is in sync; --no-escalate is a real bool flag (run.go:88); 'only rejections are escalated' and 'a failed or unparseable escalation keeps the finding' match internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:569-604 (VerdictCheckedButUnverified on error and on ParseError); 'skipped for mock runs and judges that cannot read a tree' matches wiring.go:183 and escalation.go:26.

No TODO/FIXME markers, no eval-style execution, and no truncated diff context in this shard (28590 of a 60000 budget, every chunk complete). The docs/specs 0.8.3 numbers changed in this shard (46 packs, max 60000, mean 29840) are internally consistent with the unchanged 1,372,619-byte total and with 'none over budget' since max equals the budget rather than exceeding it.

findings.note: A real git failure makes escalation silently unavailable, and a live finding is dropped -- the precise outcome the new test file asserts is impossible. changedPaths returns `(nil, nil)` when git exits nonzero with a nil error (escalation.go:86-87), and that is exactly how every git failure is reported: gate.RealExec converts *exec.ExitError into (code, nil) at gate/git.go:67-72. escalationFor then returns (nil, nil), and internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:583-585 reads that as "escalation deliberately unavailable: the rejection stands", recording VerdictHallucination -- the finding disappears. escalation_test.go:134-137 states the opposite invariant ("Every way the sandbox can fail to be built must surface as an error ... Silently returning 'unavailable' would let a broken sandbox read as agreement with the cheap arm's rejection - a finding dropped by an outage"), but both fakes in that test return os.ErrPermission in the 4th slot (escalation_test.go:140-142, 151-156), a channel git failures never use, so the assertion passes without touching the real path. Probe: an Exec fake returning `nil, []byte("fatal: bad revision"), 128, nil` for `diff` yields esc=<nil> err=<nil>. Mutation: deleting `|| code != 0` from escalation.go:86 leaves the whole ./internal/fsm/... suite green.

A nonzero `git show` exit is indistinguishable from "this path does not exist at that revision", so an unreadable object produces a partial or empty evidence tree that still carries a well-formed tree hash. showFile maps every nonzero exit to (nil, false, nil) = absent (escalation.go:106-108). With every show failing, Materialize writes nothing, returns Tree{Files:0} plus a valid-looking TreeHash, escalationFor returns it with err == nil, and the escalated codex judge is asked to settle a cross-file claim inside an EMPTY directory while the audit records evidence=sandbox and that tree hash -- a judgment attributed to evidence that was never materialized. Nothing guards against it: sandbox.Tree.Files (sandbox.go:39, incremented at :75) is read only by sandbox_test.go:53 and by no production caller, the same write-only-field pattern this very release removes from machine.CallRow (CHANGELOG.md, Fixed). Probe confirmed: tree hash f22522a2... over 0 files, no error. The subtest at escalation_test.go:148-160 pins only the err != nil path.

The materialized evidence is not the bytes at the revision, which defeats the content-addressing the feature is sold on. showFile is built on c.git, which strings.TrimSpace-es git's stdout (wiring.go:38-41) -- correct for `rev-parse`, wrong for `show`. Every file written into the sandbox therefore loses its trailing newline and any leading whitespace, and a file that is entirely whitespace materializes as empty. Probe: head/f.go contains "package f

func Added() {}" where the file at that revision is "package f

func Added() {}
". The judge reads altered source, and sandbox.TreeHash content-addresses the altered bytes, so "content-addresses it with a tree hash so a verdict stays replayable" (CHANGELOG.md) and "the recorded input stops determining the verdict; content-addressing the tree restores it" (sandbox.go package doc) do not hold against the repository the hash claims to address. Neither test in this shard can catch it: sandbox_test's ShowFunc is a fake returning exact bytes (sandbox_test.go:12-19), and escalation_test only os.Stat()s paths and never reads one (escalation_test.go:76-88) -- despite its header claiming "everything below it - git, materialization, the judge router - is the real implementation" (escalation_test.go:17-19). One assertion comparing a materialized file to `git show` output would close it.

The --no-escalate kill switch is never exercised end to end, so the flag string itself is unpinned. run.go:49 and the boolFlags entry at run.go:88 are the only wiring from the CLI flag to c.noEscalate, and no test anywhere passes the literal "--no-escalate" through parseArgs or Run: the subtest actually named "--no-escalate turns it off" assigns the struct field directly (escalation_test.go:194-199), which tests wiring.go:183 and nothing about the flag. Two mutants survive the entire ./internal/fsm/... suite: (a) changing run.go:49 to `p.bools["no-escalate-TYPO"]`, after which --no-escalate silently does nothing and every real judged run escalates -- the roughly 2x judge tokens the CHANGELOG quotes, spent against the operator's explicit instruction; (b) deleting "--no-escalate" from boolFlags, after which the flag either fails with "missing value for --no-escalate" or swallows the following argument as its value. Per the rubric this is a source change without a test that can fail.

The evidence tree is created and never removed. escalation.go:37 makes an `mrv-evidence-*` directory under TMPDIR and nothing in the repository ever deletes it -- there is no RemoveAll, no t.Cleanup, no deferred teardown on any path, including the error paths at escalation.go:42-48 that abandon an already-materialized tree. Every escalated run therefore leaves a full copy of the branch's changed files at both revisions (plus every unchanged file any finding names) on disk indefinitely, each file mode 0444; the tests leak one per escalation as well, since newHarness binds the real os.MkdirTemp. This machine currently holds 921 stray /var/folders/.../T/mrv-evidence-* directories. The directories are 0700, so this is unbounded retention of copied source rather than an exposure -- but for a feature whose stated purpose is to bound what a judge can read, copying the source out of the repository with no lifetime is the wrong default, and neither new test asserts anything about cleanup.

The case-insensitive codex prefix test is unpinned: dropping strings.ToLower from escalation.go:26 leaves the suite green, because every test model in escalation_test.go:82-92 and :171 is already lowercase. A run targeted with --judge-model Codex/gpt-5.6-sol routes to the Codex CLI (routing strips the prefix case-insensitively) but would silently never escalate. This shard's own CHANGELOG records the identical defect just fixed one guard over -- "validateCodex's empty-model guard compared against the literal lowercase prefix while routing strips it case-insensitively" -- so this is the duplicated-guard case where the copy is currently correct but nothing holds it there.

Two test-comprehension defects in the new file. escalation_test.go:219 says "seed.txt exists at HEAD and is NOT in base..head (the harness commits it first)", but the harness commits notes.md (escalation_test.go:26-31) and the assertion at :227 looks for notes.md -- seed.txt does not exist anywhere in the repository, so the comment sends a reader looking for a fixture that is not there. Separately, escalation_test.go:207 ranges over a one-element slice `[]judgeMode{judgeNone}`, which reads as a table that lost its other rows; judgeMode has exactly two values (wiring.go:137-138), so the loop is complete but the shape misleads.

The note that justifies lowering three coverage floors understates the change by 5x. tests/coverage-floor.txt:2-3 says findings/runchain/state were "lowered by ~1 statement each when the JSONL scanner moved to internal/jsonl". Measured statement totals at base (334e752) versus head: internal/state 58 -> 53, internal/runchain 107 -> 102, internal/findings 293 -> 288 -- five statements each, and five COVERED statements each, since 50/58=86.2 -> 45/53=84.9, 99/107=92.5 -> 94/102=92.2 and 272/293=92.8 -> 267/288=92.7 all reproduce the old and new floor values exactly. The cause and direction in the note are right and internal/jsonl is floored at 100.0, so nothing is actually less tested; only the magnitude claim on a gate-weakening change is wrong.
